findings.title: SPEC-00 still models SPEC-05→SPEC-04 as forbidden/indirect even though decoration persistence now requires a direct dependency
findings.location: SPEC-00 §1 Module Map; SPEC-00 §2 Seam E; SPEC-07 §2 SDR-07-012
findings.evidence: SPEC-00 Module Map lists SPEC-05 Depends On: "SPEC-01, SPEC-03, SPEC-07". Seam E says: "SPEC-03 is the sole DHF writer... SPEC-05 has no direct assembly reference to SPEC-04; the dependency is purely indirect through SPEC-03's aggregation role." But SPEC-07 SDR-07-012 says: "SPEC-05 persists this payload via SPEC-04's DhfDecorationWriter after DhfLedger.AppendTurnAsync returns the entry_id."
findings.problem: The top-level architecture contract still forbids the direct SPEC-05→SPEC-04 integration that the new decoration-persistence design requires.
findings.why_it_matters: This can make the implementation fail architecture tests, misassign ownership of retries/circuit breaker/LockSessionAsync, and leave reviewers enforcing the wrong dependency rule.
findings.proposed_fix: Update SPEC-00 to add the direct SPEC-05→SPEC-04 dependency explicitly, split entry writes from decoration writes, and name the exact allowed SPEC-04 surface SPEC-05 may call after AppendTurnAsync returns.

findings.title: GetFeatureTree wire contract still cannot express the adapter's compressed/full feature-tree choice
findings.location: SPEC-01 §7.1 GetFeatureTreeInput; SPEC-02 §3.4 ISolidWorksFeatureService.GetFeatureTree; Changed Sections Since Last Round
findings.evidence: SPEC-01 defines `public record GetFeatureTreeInput : IToolInput { public bool IncludeSuppressed { get; init; } = false; }`. SPEC-02 defines `IReadOnlyList<FeatureNode> GetFeatureTree(bool includeSuppressed, bool compressed);`. The changed-sections list claims: "SPEC-01 §7.1 GetFeatureTreeInput (Compressed field added)".
findings.problem: The cross-process tool input still lacks the `Compressed` selector required by the add-in-side service contract.
findings.why_it_matters: The orchestrator cannot deterministically request compressed vs full feature trees over the wire, so producer and consumer can both follow their local specs and still disagree at runtime.
findings.proposed_fix: Either add `Compressed` to SPEC-01 `GetFeatureTreeInput` and propagate it through validators/schema/tests, or remove the `compressed` parameter from SPEC-02 and define one fixed behavior system-wide.

findings.title: SPEC-02 still emits an unsupported `FeatureTreeHash = "OVERSIZE"` sentinel in the oversize path
findings.location: SPEC-02 §7.5 Full Message-Size Check; SPEC-01 §8 State Snapshot
findings.evidence: SPEC-02 says the oversize fallback uses a placeholder state with `FeatureTreeHash = "OVERSIZE"`. SPEC-01 §8 says: "The `FeatureTreeHash` MUST still reflect the hash of the complete (non-truncated) tree so that change detection remains accurate."
findings.problem: The oversize fallback invents a hash sentinel that is not part of the wire contract and directly violates the `StateSnapshot` hash invariant.
findings.why_it_matters: Downstream reconciliation, change detection, and any validator assuming `FeatureTreeHash` is a real hash become unreliable exactly on the failure path where accurate recovery data matters most.
findings.proposed_fix: Use the real hash of the complete untruncated tree even in the oversize placeholder state, or formally add a supported sentinel to SPEC-01 and update all validators/consumers accordingly.

findings.title: The teardown-send threading model is internally contradictory
findings.location: SPEC-02 §9.0.2 SendTeardownAsync pseudocode; SPEC-02 §9.0.3 trigger orchestration note; SPEC-02 §9.1.1 step 3
findings.evidence: §9.0.2 shows direct network I/O: `await _webSocket.SendAsync(...)`. §9.0.3 says teardown send would "block behind the COM call on the shared message queue (both go through `SwUiThreadCommandQueue`)". §9.1.1 step 3 says: "Do NOT attempt to send `AddinTeardownMessage`. The send path goes through `SwUiThreadCommandQueue`..."
findings.problem: The failure-mode reasoning assumes teardown send is UI-thread-queued, while the pseudocode defines it as direct WebSocket I/O.
findings.why_it_matters: Closure attribution (`explicit_shutdown` vs `heartbeat_timeout`) and the entire stuck-call escalation behavior depend on which model is true.
findings.proposed_fix: Pick one mechanism and make all teardown sections consistent: either explicitly route sends off the UI thread and allow best-effort send during escalation, or document the UI-thread dependency concretely and remove the direct-send pseudocode.

findings.title: [speculative] NetFx handshake classification still depends on HTTP upgrade details the spec does not show how to observe
findings.evidence: The add-in behavior is specified as `WebSocketException with HTTP 401`, `HTTP 400`, and `HTTP 429 -> back off per Retry-After header` while the add-in target is `.NET Framework 4.8` using `ClientWebSocket`.
findings.problem: [speculative] The document assumes the add-in can reliably read upgrade-response status codes and headers from `ClientWebSocket.ConnectAsync`, but it does not define the mechanism and NetFx may not expose them cleanly.
findings.why_it_matters: If those details are not observable, auth failures can be misclassified as transient network faults, leading to wrong retry behavior and bad UX.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify the exact NetFx client API/library that exposes upgrade-response status/headers, or add a preflight HTTPS probe/fallback classification path when handshake details are unavailable.

findings.title: Day-0 validation still tells operators to inspect a DHF closure reason that no longer exists in the schema
findings.location: SPEC-02 §11 Day-0 Validation item 11; SPEC-00 changelog C3; SPEC-00 §6 Glossary
findings.evidence: SPEC-02 item 11 says: "confirm the orchestrator's DHF session row shows closure reason `explicit_shutdown`". SPEC-00 C3 says closure reason is "recorded in orchestrator structured logs ... NOT in the DHF schema".
findings.problem: The validation procedure points reviewers at a persistence location the architecture explicitly removed.
findings.why_it_matters: This makes a required go/no-go check impossible to execute as written and creates false debugging churn around nonexistent DHF columns.
findings.proposed_fix: Change item 11 to verify `ended_at` in `dhf.sessions` and the structured Serilog `session_closed` event separately; remove any DHF-row closure-reason check.

findings.title: The viewer raw-input gate is referenced but not present in the documented options or config surface
findings.location: SPEC-06 §2 SDR-06-008; SPEC-06 §3 ViewerOptions; SPEC-06 §13 Configuration
findings.evidence: SDR-06-008 references `ViewerOptions.VocabRawInputAllowed`, but the `ViewerOptions` snippet only defines `EnableStretchEndpoints`, and the config example only shows `"enableStretchEndpoints": true`.
findings.problem: The spec names a configuration switch that the documented option type and config block do not expose.
findings.why_it_matters: Implementers cannot tell what key to wire, testers cannot verify the role gate, and deployments may invent incompatible config names.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the raw-input gate to the `ViewerOptions` type and the config section with an explicit default and consumption path, or remove the option name until the surface is formally defined.

findings.title: The documented 'per-tenant' raw-input override cannot be implemented by a single viewer-wide boolean
findings.evidence: SDR-06-008 says the token is "provisioned per-tenant at deployment time as a tenant-level configuration flag (`ViewerOptions.VocabRawInputAllowed`)" and that a "tenant-specific override to true" enables raw-input display for that tenant's sessions.
findings.problem: A single global `ViewerOptions` flag cannot represent different values for different tenants.
findings.why_it_matters: The privacy/governance model is stronger than the documented config model can actually enforce; in practice the setting becomes all-tenants-or-none.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a tenant-scoped policy source (e.g., per-tenant allowlist/mapping keyed by tenantId) or explicitly downgrade the behavior to a global switch until authenticated per-user claims exist.

findings.title: SPEC-07 still states that SPEC-07 pipeline success waits for durable citation persistence, which contradicts the v1.1.2 ownership shift
findings.location: SPEC-07 §0; SPEC-07 §2 SDR-07-006; SPEC-07 §3.1 Stage 5; SPEC-07 §2 SDR-07-012
findings.evidence: §0 says: "The pipeline returns success ONLY after the citation is durably written." SDR-07-006 says: "The write is awaited on the critical path... pipeline success is reported only after durable persistence." But Stage 5 now says: "NOT persisted here — returned to SPEC-05" and SDR-07-012 says persistence happens in SPEC-05 after `AppendTurnAsync` returns `entry_id`.
findings.problem: The normative success condition still belongs to the pre-C1 architecture even though persistence moved out of SPEC-07.
findings.why_it_matters: Callers cannot tell whether a `PipelineResult` means 'payload assembled' or 'citation durably stored', so cross-module behavior and tests will diverge.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite §0 and SDR-07-006 so SPEC-07 guarantees payload assembly only; move the durable-write success condition entirely into SPEC-05/SPEC-04 integration text.

findings.title: SPEC-07 still disagrees with itself about whether rejected security events create a DHF decoration
findings.location: SPEC-07 §3.3 Failure Modes; SPEC-07 §14 Failure Mode Taxonomy
findings.evidence: In §3.3, the row for "Bouncer rejects utterance" says `Decoration Written?` = "Only if `security_event=true`". The note below says "no DHF decoration is written for rejections — security events route to the restricted audit sink". §14 says security-event rejection => `No (security events logged, not DHF'd)`.
findings.problem: The document still contains two incompatible rules for the same security-event path.
findings.why_it_matters: One implementation path may write attacker-controlled content into DHF while another assumes those events never enter the append-only audit chain.
findings.proposed_fix: Choose one rule and update every table/test consistently; if the intended rule is audit-sink-only, change all security-event rejection rows to `Decoration Written? No`.

findings.title: SPEC-07 `StageLatencies` still requires `DecorationWriteMs` and `TotalMs` even though SPEC-07 returns before any write occurs
findings.location: SPEC-07 §6.4 StageLatencies/PipelineResult; SPEC-07 §3.1 Stage 5; SPEC-07 §3.2 Latency Budget
findings.evidence: `StageLatencies` requires `DecorationWriteMs` and `TotalMs`, and `PipelineResult` requires `Latencies`. But Stage 5 now only assembles a decoration payload and returns it to SPEC-05, and §3.2 removed decoration write time from SPEC-07's end-to-end budget.
findings.problem: SPEC-07 cannot populate required latency fields at the point it returns `PipelineResult`.
findings.why_it_matters: The DTO is internally impossible as specified; implementations must either invent values or violate the required-field contract.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove `DecorationWriteMs` and `TotalMs` from SPEC-07 `StageLatencies`, or split SPEC-07 pipeline timing from SPEC-05 persistence timing into separate DTOs with separate owners.

top_3_must_fix: SPEC-07 C1 migration is incomplete: §0/SDR-07-006 still promise durable writes in SPEC-07, and `StageLatencies` still requires post-write fields.
SPEC-00 still omits the direct SPEC-05→SPEC-04 seam required for decoration persistence, so the top-level dependency contract rejects the new architecture.
The feature-tree contracts are still broken across SPEC-01/02: `GetFeatureTreeInput` lacks `Compressed`, and SPEC-02 still emits unsupported `FeatureTreeHash = "OVERSIZE"`.
